items.title: Harry Fairconnetue Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: Yeah, that's when they had the family band. That was the family band. Oh, uh, Sosia band.

ctx.x: But did you, in those times when you were playing with Maurice and Collins, did you play in the

Bay St. Louis past Christian, or did you go up to Jackson, or did you go to... Bay St. Louis, from Bay St. Louis to Forrest Biloxi. From Forrest Biloxi. That's Forrest Biloxi. And you didn't go west? No, I never did go west. In those days? In those days, uh-huh. And from Bay St. Louis out in the kiln, Kiln, Prelton. And uh, that's about the footage out there. In those days. Uh-huh. Well, uh, I heard you, you know, you mentioned different ones playing with, uh, what was one of the bands you was playing over here…

Regular dance jobs. They could stay up late enough to play dance, huh? Oh, yeah. Four hours. Do they have dances in the daytime level? Not hardly. Not hardly. I just thought there might be some kind of special jobs that kids could play during the daytime. No, not hardly. Never played ball games or anything like that. No.
